content:
SAMUEL ACHTERBERG-OSEI
Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer
samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud and infrastructure engineer with experience operating Azure environments, developing Terraform modules, automating deployments and administering Windows and Linux servers. Background includes cloud networking, security, Azure migrations and freelance IT administration.

SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: Azure VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure AD / Entra ID, Azure Monitor, Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL)
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Bicep, Ansible, PowerShell, Bash
DevOps and containers: Azure DevOps Pipelines, Docker, Kubernetes (AKS)
Networking and security: TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, MFA, conditional access
Administration: Active Directory, Microsoft 365

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V.
Mar 2025 – Present
- Operate the company’s Azure estate as part of a three-person cloud team, supporting approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions.
- Developed Terraform modules for landing-zone networking, including hub-spoke VNets, Azure Firewall and private endpoints.
- Moved release pipelines for 15 internal applications from manual deployments to Azure DevOps YAML pipelines.

Freelance IT Administrator | Self-employed, small businesses
Sep 2022 – Jan 2024
- Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for nine small businesses with 5–40 employees.
- Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint and OneDrive.
- Set up backups and basic security baselines, including MFA and conditional access.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Jan 2014 – Feb 2020
- Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
- Led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS in 2019.
- Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
- Provided second-line escalation support for network and Active Directory issues.

Helpdesk Technician | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Aug 2011 – Dec 2013

EDUCATION
MBO 4 IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College | 2011

CERTIFICATIONS
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) | 2019
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003) | 2025

LANGUAGES
Dutch: Native | English: Fluent | Twi: Spoken

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professionally structured, and easy to scan. It presents strong quantified infrastructure experience, including approximately 400 VMs, 12 AKS clusters, 15 application pipelines, and a 60-server Azure migration. The progression from Helpdesk Technician to Cloud Engineer is credible. The main content limitation is that several claims relevant to this role are presented as broad keywords rather than demonstrated responsibilities: systems architecture, technical proposals, stakeholder communication, observability, reliability, and end-to-end ownership. The CV also does not explicitly distinguish infrastructure design from administration or operation.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, conventional dates, and ATS-friendly keyword groupings. It should parse well and has a good AI-screening probability for Azure, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, networking, security, and infrastructure operations. Alignment would improve if supported job terminology such as “hands-on infrastructure engineering,” “cloud environment design and operation,” “systems architecture,” “technical leadership,” “infrastructure as code,” and “technical communication” were incorporated into the summary and experience bullets. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, IoT, backend, or JVM keywords because they are not supported by the Original Candidate Information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a strong match for hands-on Azure infrastructure engineering, cloud operation, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, Linux and virtual machines, networking, and practical security. The Azure migration, landing-zone networking, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, and pipeline work are relevant to a platform being taken into production. The largest genuine gaps are Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, train/vehicle or IoT integration, backend/full-stack development, and AWS. The document provides some evidence of technical leadership through leading the 60-server migration, but it does not establish experience leading cross-team technical proposals or bringing external stakeholders along. It also does not explicitly demonstrate observability, telemetry ingestion, video streaming, remote-device connectivity, or backend service deployment. Azure is acceptable under the requirement allowing other major clouds.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL/KEY ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the current summary with a more role-aligned version using only supported evidence: “Cloud and infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing, operating and automating Azure environments, including approximately 400 VMs, 12 AKS clusters and three subscriptions. Experienced in Terraform-based infrastructure as code, landing-zone networking, Azure migrations, Windows and Linux administration, security baselines and Azure DevOps deployment automation. Led a 60-server VMware-to-Azure IaaS migration and technical infrastructure improvements from implementation through operation.” This adds the job’s supported terminology without claiming Terragrunt, mTLS, IoT, backend, or AWS experience.
2. In the Skills section, rename “Infrastructure as code and automation” to “Infrastructure as Code and Automation” and place “Terraform” first. Keep “Bicep, Ansible, PowerShell, Bash” after it. Do not add Terragrunt, since it is not present in the Original Candidate Information.
3. In the Professional Experience section under “Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V.,” revise the first bullet to: “Operate and support Azure cloud infrastructure across three subscriptions, including approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters, as part of a three-person cloud team.” This directly reflects “cloud environment design and operation” while remaining truthful.
4. Under Havenstad Logistics, revise the Terraform bullet to: “Developed Terraform modules for landing-zone networking, including hub-spoke VNets, Azure Firewall and private endpoints, supporting repeatable and secure Azure infrastructure deployment.” The phrase “repeatable and secure” is supported by the infrastructure-as-code and security work described, and improves alignment with the employer’s infrastructure repository and security focus.
5. Under “Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services,” revise the migration bullet to: “Led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware-hosted servers to Azure IaaS in 2019, coordinating the infrastructure move through implementation.” Use “coordinating” only if the candidate’s leadership involved coordination; otherwise retain the current wording and use: “Led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware-hosted servers to Azure IaaS in 2019.” This is the strongest existing evidence for technical leadership and systems implementation.
6. Under the same Systems Administrator role, combine the networking and Active Directory evidence into a more searchable bullet: “Provided second-line escalation support for networking and Active Directory issues, including TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls and user administration.” This uses skills already listed and makes the networking experience more explicit.
7. In the Skills section under “Networking and security,” retain “TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, MFA, conditional access” and add “security baselines” because it is explicitly supported by the freelance experience. Do not add mTLS or SSL/TLS; these are genuine experience gaps, not wording omissions.
8. In the Professional Summary or Skills section, include “Azure migrations” and “Azure DevOps YAML pipelines” exactly as supported terms. These are currently present in substance but should be surfaced as searchable phrases because they are relevant to taking infrastructure into production.

MINOR ATS/CLARITY IMPROVEMENTS
9. In the header, use the original location format if desired—“Rotterdam, Netherlands”—because it is present in the Original CV and provides complete contact context. Keep the header as plain text and avoid tables, icons, text boxes, or graphics.
10. In the Certifications section, retain the full certification names and identifiers exactly as written. These are valuable ATS terms and are already correctly presented.
